name: hip_grouped_gemm_via_fwd_tile_reuse
description: Turn a production HIP single-GEMM into a grouped-GEMM (MoE) by wrapping its tile struct with per-expert flat-grid dispatch — no kernel-body rewrite. Inherits all register pinning, AGPR use, LDS double-buffering, and waitcnt tuning of the reference.
preconditions: An existing HIP single-GEMM kernel that exposes its tile work as a templated struct (e.g., GEMM_Tile_MXFP8_NT_256x256x128_...)
The tile struct encapsulates LDS setup, load helpers, phase functions, and register pins, so the kernel body is mostly a sequence of tile.method calls
Caller can supply group_offs, block_to_expert, and tile_offs tensors (host-precomputed)
steps: Copy the single-GEMM kernel body verbatim into a new grouped kernel
Replace the (m, n) boundary computation: pid_m/pid_n now come from block_to_expert + tile_offs lookup, not swizzle_pid_m_n
Replace global m with per-expert m_g = group_offs[g+1] - group_offs[g]
Shift base pointers: a_base += group_offs[g] * K; b_base += g * N * K (NT) or g * K * N (NN); c_base += group_offs[g] * N
Keep tile pipeline phases unchanged — they see the same extents
Host side: compute block_to_expert = repeat_interleave(arange(G), tiles_per_expert)
expected_impact: Inherit the compute-side wins of the reference kernel (e.g., 27 s_waitcnt / 512 MFMA = 0.053 waitcnt/MFMA vs Triton's ~0.875) for ~500 lines of delta, no tuning effort. On gpt_oss_20B MoE gate_up: fwd 1.131× / dgrad 1.274× Triton with zero kernel-body edits.
decision_rules: Use when you have a tuned single-GEMM kernel and need its grouped-MoE variant.
Per-expert data constraints (e.g., M_g % preshuffle_block == 0) must hold — preshuffle operates globally, and non-aligned group starts break scale layout.
Do NOT refactor the kernel body to call through a helper — the tight register pinning breaks on inlining changes. Copy-paste is correct here.
